questions.title: The screen's job is clear from the first screen
questions.why: The title 'Confirm your card' promises a match to confirm, but the screen shows 'No photo found' and 'We couldn't find a confident match' instead.

questions.title: The action that does the job stands out most
questions.why: The red 'No photo found — go back…' banner draws the eye first, while the actual ways forward ('Search for your card', the game tiles) have no single primary.

questions.title: Every label says what happens when tapped
questions.why: 'One Piece', 'Pokémon', 'Other cards' and the search placeholder 'Character, card number, or set' say what each does.

questions.title: No terms this user wouldn't know
questions.why: 'confident match' and 'card database' in 'We couldn't find a confident match in our card database' are system language, not seller language.

questions.title: Only asks what this user can decide at this stage
questions.why: Searching by character/number or picking a game are things the seller knows.

questions.title: Advanced detail is tucked away
questions.why: Only three game tiles are shown up front.

questions.title: Everything fits this stage and this user
questions.why: Everything is about identifying the card.

questions.title: Little reading needed to act
questions.why: Three stacked messages (the red error, 'Search for your card', the no-match line) must be read before the seller knows what to do.
